explanation: Boston newspapers of the late 1830s loved jokey abbreviations. OK spread in 1840, when supporters of Martin Van Buren, nicknamed Old Kinderhook, used it as a campaign slogan.

claims.text: The word OK originated as an abbreviation of 'oll korrect', a humorous misspelling of 'all correct'.
OK first appeared in print in a Boston newspaper in 1839, during a fashion for joke abbreviations.
OK spread during the 1840 US presidential campaign, when supporters of Martin Van Buren used it for his nickname, Old Kinderhook.
